property_summary: For any inputs to initialize, the reference implementation sets the contract's baseToken to the provided _baseToken argument; the mutant erroneously sets baseToken to address(0) regardless, so for some fuzzed _baseToken values the post-initialize baseToken will differ (the reference equals the argument, the mutant does not).

For any initialize(...) input the reference contract sets baseToken to the _baseToken argument (c.baseToken() == _baseToken) after initialize returns; the mutant sets baseToken to the factory address instead, so there exist inputs where c.baseToken() != _baseToken.

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's public getter baseToken() equals the _baseToken argument passed (reference preserves baseToken = _baseToken), whereas the mutant incorrectly sets baseToken to the nft address for some inputs causing baseToken() != _baseToken.

For any initialize(...) call the reference contract sets baseToken equal to the _baseToken argument (i.e. c.baseToken() == _baseToken after initialize); the mutant flips non-zero inputs to address(0) causing c.baseToken() != _baseToken for some inputs.
After initialize(...) completes successfully, the contract's public nft() equals the _nft argument passed to initialize; the mutant sets nft to address(0) and therefore violates this for some inputs.

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's nft getter returns the provided _nft address (i.e. nft == _nft) after successful initialize; the mutant assigns nft = tx.origin and therefore can produce a mismatch for some calls.

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's nft getter equals the _nft argument passed (i.e., initialize sets nft = _nft); the mutant sets nft = msg.sender so for some inputs nft != _nft and the property is violated.

For every input to initialize(...), the reference contract sets the stored changeFee equal to the _changeFee argument passed (changeFee == _changeFee); the mutant increments before storing (changeFee == _changeFee + 1) and thus will violate this rule for inputs where _changeFee is not already maximal and observable.

For any inputs to initialize(...), after a successful call the contract's public changeFee equals the _changeFee argument passed; the mutant that forces changeFee to 0 violates this when _changeFee != 0.

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's stored changeFee equals the _changeFee argument provided (i.e. changeFee == _changeFee); the mutant doubles the stored value so for some fuzzed _changeFee the equality will fail.
For all inputs, the reference contract reverts when initialize is called with feeRate > 5000 (enforcing FeeRateTooHigh), whereas the mutant allows such calls to succeed and set feeRate > 5000.

For any inputs to initialize the reference contract sets feeRate to the provided _feeRate (observable via public getter) regardless of ordering, but the mutant that swaps the assignment order can cause feeRate to differ (i.e., not equal to the passed _feeRate) for some inputs due to the different write ordering being observable), so assert that c.feeRate() == _feeRate after initialize; the mutant will fail this for some fuzzed inputs.

After initialize(...) returns, the feeRate public getter must equal the _feeRate argument for all inputs; the mutant that swaps writing feeRate/changeFee can cause feeRate() to differ from the supplied _feeRate for some fuzzed inputs, so the property is feeRate() == _feeRate.

After any call to initialize(...) the contract's public feeRate getter must equal the _feeRate argument passed; the mutant that swaps assignments can make feeRate() differ for some inputs (due to storage write ordering observable via emitted Initialize event reading the parameters), so this property will hold for the reference but be violated by the mutant for some fuzzed inputs.

For all inputs, calling initialize(...) sets the public feeRate getter to the value passed in as the _feeRate argument and the emitted Initialize event's feeRate argument equals that same _feeRate; the mutant that swaps assignments can make the stored feeRate differ from the emitted event parameter for some inputs (observable mismatch between getter and last emitted Initialize event field).

For every call to initialize(...) the reference contract's public feeRate equals the value returned by the Initialize event's second-to-last numeric argument (the emitted _feeRate argument), whereas the mutant swapping the assignment order can make the stored feeRate differ from the emitted _feeRate for some inputs — so the rule: after initialize returns, c.feeRate() == the _feeRate argument encoded in the emitted Initialize event payload.
